# storybook-vrhythm

> Baseline grid for Storybook 10 and 11. Measures stories against the grid and reports each off-grid edge with an exact pixel delta, so coding agents can fix alignment without screenshots. Also draws the grid as an overlay. Zero runtime dependencies. Framework agnostic.

## Agent quick start

Do not judge a screenshot of the overlay. Use the audit's numbers.

1. Install: `npx storybook add storybook-vrhythm@next`. Always use `@next`, also on Storybook 10: `latest` is 0.x and has no audit.
2. Make sure the project runs story tests in a real browser: `@storybook/addon-vitest` with Playwright. Install it with `npx storybook add @storybook/addon-vitest` if missing. jsdom has no layout.
3. Set the grid and turn on the audit, inside the default-exported object of `.storybook/preview.ts`, or in one component's `parameters`:

```typescript
const preview = {
  parameters: {
    vrhythm: { lineHeight: '8px', audit: 'error' },
  },
};

export default preview;
```

4. Run the tests: `npx vitest run path/to/Component.stories.tsx`, or the `test-run` tool of `@storybook/addon-mcp`.
5. Follow the fix workflow in "Auditing rhythm".

Rules:

- Do not raise `tolerance`, lower `lineHeight`, remove the audit or delete an assertion to get a pass.
- Add `data-vrhythm-ignore` only to elements that are off-grid on purpose, and tell the user why.

An Agent Skill with the same workflow ships at `node_modules/storybook-vrhythm/skills/`.

## Overview

`storybook-vrhythm` is a Storybook addon with two parts. `storybook-vrhythm/audit` measures elements against a baseline grid. The overlay draws that grid with a CSS `linear-gradient`. It is non-interactive (`pointer-events: none`) and toggleable via the toolbar.

Supported frameworks: React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Web Components, HTML.

## Installation

```bash
npx storybook add storybook-vrhythm@next
```

This installs the addon and registers it. By hand: `pnpm add -D storybook-vrhythm@next` and Option A below.

Requirements: Node.js 22.12+, Storybook 10 or 11. Use the `next` tag on both. The `latest` tag is 0.x: it supports Storybook 10 only and has no `storybook-vrhythm/audit`.

## Setup

### Option A: Addon preset (recommended)

Add to `.storybook/main.ts`:

```typescript
export default {
  addons: ['storybook-vrhythm'],
};
```

This automatically registers the decorator and toolbar toggle for all stories.

### Option B: CSF Next

```typescript
// .storybook/preview.ts
import { definePreview } from '@storybook/your-framework';
import vrhythm from 'storybook-vrhythm';

export default definePreview({
  addons: [vrhythm()],
});
```

This registers the same decorator and toolbar toggle, with typed `parameters.vrhythm`. No `.storybook/main.ts` entry is needed.

`definePreview` must come from your framework package. `@storybook/html` and `@storybook/html-vite` 11.0.0-beta.0 don't export it, so use Option A for HTML projects.

### Option C: Manual decorator

```typescript
// .storybook/preview.ts
import { withVRhythm } from 'storybook-vrhythm';

const preview = {
  decorators: [withVRhythm],
};

export default preview;
```

The `audit` parameter needs Option A or B. The manual decorator only draws the grid.

## Configuration

Parameters are passed via `parameters.vrhythm` at the story or global level.

### Global defaults (.storybook/preview.ts)

```typescript
const preview = {
  parameters: {
    vrhythm: {
      lineHeight: '8px',
      color: 'rgba(0, 150, 255, 0.2)',
    },
  },
};

export default preview;
```

Put `parameters` inside the default export. A separate `export const parameters` next to `export default preview` is ignored, with no error. With `definePreview`, put it in the object passed to `definePreview`.

### Off by default

The overlay shows on every story after install. `initialGlobals: { vrhythm: 'false' }` in the default-exported preview object keeps it off until someone picks it in the toolbar. This also keeps it out of visual regression tests such as Chromatic. The `audit` parameter still runs.

### Per-story

```typescript
export const MyStory = {
  parameters: {
    vrhythm: {
      preset: 'material',
    },
  },
};

export const Hidden = {
  parameters: {
    vrhythm: { hide: true },
  },
};
```

## Style Parameters

| Parameter     | Type               | Default                | Description                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `color`       | `string`           | `'rgb(204, 204, 204)'` | CSS color for horizontal guide lines               |
| `lineHeight`  | `string \| number` | `'16px'`               | Baseline grid height (e.g. `'8px'`, `'1rem'`)      |
| `lineWidth`   | `string \| number` | `'1px'`                | Thickness of each horizontal guide line            |
| `offset`      | `string \| number` | `0`                    | Vertical offset from the anchor                    |
| `opacity`     | `number`           | `1`                    | Overlay opacity (0–1)                              |
| `zIndex`      | `number`           | `9999`                 | Stack order of the overlay                         |
| `maxWidth`    | `string \| number` | —                      | Centers the overlay horizontally at this max width |
| `columnWidth` | `string \| number` | —                      | Repeating column width for vertical column grid    |
| `columnColor` | `string`           | —                      | Color for column lines (falls back to `color`)     |
| `gutterWidth` | `string \| number` | —                      | Gutter between columns (requires `columnWidth`)    |

## Config Parameters

| Parameter      | Type                          | Default   | Description                                                        |
| -------------- | ----------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `audit`        | `'error' \| 'todo' \| 'off'`  | `'off'`   | Audit the story after it renders and after `play`. `'error'` fails it, `'todo'` warns in the console |
| `auditOptions` | `AuditOptions`                | —         | Options for that audit. `lineHeight` defaults to the story's grid  |
| `anchor`       | `'story' \| 'page' \| string` | `'story'` | Where the first grid line starts: story root, document top, or a selector looked up after render. Docs pages always use `'page'` |
| `hide`         | `boolean`                     | `false`   | Hide the overlay for this story (overrides toolbar toggle)         |
| `preset`       | `string`                      | —         | Built-in preset name. An unknown name warns, and the audit rejects it |
| `container`    | `string`                      | —         | Deprecated: use `anchor`, which takes the same selector            |

## Built-in Presets

Pass `preset` in `parameters.vrhythm` to use a ready-made configuration.

| Preset name | lineHeight | color                       | Use case                  |
| ----------- | ---------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `4px`       | 4px        | `rgba(0, 150, 255, 0.15)`  | Dense UIs, compact grids  |
| `8px`       | 8px        | `rgba(0, 150, 255, 0.2)`   | Standard 8pt grid         |
| `12px`      | 12px       | `rgba(0, 150, 255, 0.2)`   | 12px grids, mid-density UIs |
| `16px`      | 16px       | `rgba(204, 204, 204, 0.5)` | Body text baseline        |
| `24px`      | 24px       | `rgba(204, 204, 204, 0.5)` | Heading alignment         |
| `32px`      | 32px       | `rgba(204, 204, 204, 0.5)` | Large-scale layout grids  |

Aliases: these names add no style of their own. Each one is exactly the base preset shown, under a name you may recognize from a design system:

| Alias       | Same as | Reason                                    |
| ----------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `material`  | `4px`   | Material Design uses a 4dp grid           |
| `tailwind`  | `4px`   | Tailwind's spacing unit is 0.25rem        |
| `bootstrap` | `24px`  | Body text is 1rem × 1.5 line-height       |
| `carbon`    | `8px`   | IBM Carbon uses an 8px mini-unit          |

## Exports

```typescript
import { withVRhythm, presets } from 'storybook-vrhythm';
import type { VRhythmParams, StyleProps, ConfigProps, PresetName } from 'storybook-vrhythm';
```

- `withVRhythm` — Storybook `DecoratorFunction` that injects the overlay
- `presets` — record of all built-in preset configurations
- `presetAliases` — record mapping each alias (`material`, `tailwind`, `bootstrap`, `carbon`) to its base preset
- `VRhythmParams` — `StyleProps & ConfigProps` (all parameters combined)
- `StyleProps` — visual style parameters
- `ConfigProps` — behavior parameters (`audit`, `auditOptions`, `anchor`, `hide`, `preset`, `container`)
- `PresetName` — union type of valid preset names (`'4px' | '8px' | '12px' | '16px' | '24px' | '32px' | 'material' | 'tailwind' | 'bootstrap' | 'carbon'`)

```typescript
import { auditRhythm, expectRhythm } from 'storybook-vrhythm/audit';
import { RhythmErrorCode } from 'storybook-vrhythm/audit';
import type { AuditOptions, RhythmAssertionError, RhythmConfigError, RhythmReport, RhythmViolation } from 'storybook-vrhythm/audit';
```

- `auditRhythm(root, options?)` — async, returns a `RhythmReport`: `{ ok, grid: { lineHeight, origin }, checked, violations }`
- `expectRhythm(root, options?)` — async, throws `RhythmAssertionError` (with `.report`) when elements are off-grid or nothing was measured
- `RhythmAssertionError` — type of that error: `Error & { code, report: RhythmReport }`
- `RhythmConfigError` — type of the error for setups the audit cannot judge: `Error & { code }`
- `RhythmErrorCode` — map of stable error codes. Branch on `error.code`, not on the message
- `RhythmViolation` — `{ selector, edge: 'top' | 'bottom' | 'baseline', actual, nearest, delta }`

## Auditing rhythm

Use the audit to check alignment without judging a screenshot. It needs a real browser: jsdom has no layout. Full details: https://github.com/jmlweb/storybook-vrhythm/blob/main/packages/storybook-vrhythm/README.md#auditing-rhythm-in-tests

Workflow for fixing layout:

1. Set `audit: 'error'` in `parameters.vrhythm`. For one story, add `await expectRhythm(canvasElement)` to its `play` function, or call `auditRhythm(canvasElement)` for data.
2. Run the story's tests.
3. Fix the first violation in the output by moving its edge by `-delta` pixels. A `delta` of `-3` means the edge is 3px above the nearest grid line.
4. Rerun after each fix. Moving an edge shifts everything below it, so later `delta` values go stale and on-grid edges can move off.

The failure message lists violations with equal `delta` together: a pattern, not proof of a shared cause. It shows 10 at most. `error.report.violations` has them all.

Gradual adoption: `audit: 'todo'` first, then `audit: 'error'` with `auditOptions: { edges: ['top'] }`, then the default edges.

Options: `lineHeight` and `offset` (default: read from the overlay), `anchor` (default `root`), `tolerance` (default `0.5`), `checks` (default `['box']`), `edges` (default both), `ignore` (selector).

- `edges: ['top']` skips bottom edges, so it misses a wrong height.
- `checked` counts what was measured after `checks`, `edges` and `ignore` apply. `0` means nothing was tested.
- The grid starts at the story root, so `centered`, `padded` and `fullscreen` give the same result at any viewport height. A top margin on the first element collapses through the root and moves it, so that margin is not measured.

- `checks: ['box']` measures element top and bottom edges. Use it for spacing grids (4px, 8px).
- `checks: ['baseline']` measures text baselines. Use it for type-driven grids only: text on a spacing grid fails it by design.
- Add `data-vrhythm-ignore` when the component is off-grid on purpose. It skips the element and its subtree.
- Use the `ignore` option to skip a selector and its subtree for one story, or without touching markup.
- `grid.origin` is the viewport Y of the first grid line, also printed in the failure message. `actual` and `nearest` are relative to it. It is the overlay's top, or the top of `root` plus `offset` when `offset` is set or the overlay is hidden.
- With a hidden overlay, the `audit` parameter uses the grid the overlay would have drawn. `expectRhythm` and `auditRhythm` need `lineHeight` from you, or they throw `No grid found`. Pass `anchor` or `offset` to set the origin.
- `audit: 'error'` fails with `NOTHING_MEASURED` when nothing was measured. Set `audit: 'off'` on stories that render outside the canvas, such as portals. `audit: 'todo'` never fails a story: it warns about off-grid edges and bad setups alike.
- A preset picked in the toolbar overrides the story's style params, including the grid the audit reads from the overlay.
- Audit option `offset` starts at `root`, or at the `anchor` audit option. The story's `offset` starts at the story's anchor.
- `RhythmConfigError` means no real answer was possible. Fix the setup; do not catch it.

Error codes (`error.code`):

| `code` | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `OFF_GRID` | Run the fix workflow |
| `NOTHING_MEASURED` | `root` is empty or there is no layout: run in a real browser, check the story renders |
| `NO_GRID` | No overlay: pass `lineHeight`, or register the addon |
| `UNKNOWN_PRESET` | Fix the `preset` name |
| `ANCHOR_NOT_FOUND` | Fix the `anchor` selector |
| `UNUSABLE_OVERLAY` | The overlay has no area or lies outside `root`: check `offset`, `anchor`, `maxWidth` |
| `INVALID_LENGTH` | `lineHeight` or `offset` is not a finite `px` or `rem` length, or `lineHeight` is 0 or less |
| `INVALID_TOLERANCE` | `tolerance` is negative, not finite, or half of `lineHeight` or more |
| `INVALID_EDGES` | `edges` is empty |
| `UNMEASURABLE` | The environment cannot measure an edge or baseline: run in a real browser |

## Toolbar Globals

The addon registers a `vrhythm` global with these toolbar values:

| Value        | Behavior                                      |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `'true'`     | Use story-level parameters (default)          |
| `'false'`    | Hide the overlay                              |
| `'4px'`      | Override with 4px preset                     |
| `'8px'`      | Override with 8px preset                     |
| `'12px'`     | Override with 12px preset                    |
| `'16px'`     | Override with 16px preset                    |
| `'24px'`     | Override with 24px preset                    |
| `'32px'`     | Override with 32px preset                    |
| `'material'` | Alias of `'4px'`                              |
| `'tailwind'` | Alias of `'4px'`                              |
| `'bootstrap'`| Alias of `'24px'`                             |
| `'carbon'`   | Alias of `'8px'`                              |

Story-level `hide: true` always overrides the toolbar toggle.

## How it works

1. A `<div id="storybook-rhythm">` is injected into the DOM (or reused if already present)
2. Its `background` is set to a `linear-gradient` that repeats at `lineHeight` intervals
3. If `columnWidth` is set, a second `linear-gradient(90deg, ...)` layer creates vertical columns
4. The div stays on `body`, positioned `absolute` with `pointer-events: none`, so it never interferes with stories
5. It starts at the anchor plus `offset`, runs to the end of the document, and follows resizes. Content that scrolls inside its own container has no grid past the first screen, but the audit is not affected
6. On hide, the div is removed from the DOM entirely

## TypeScript

`parameters.vrhythm` is type-checked when the addon is registered through `definePreview`. With `addons: ['storybook-vrhythm']`, `StoryObj` does not check it, so an invalid value only shows at runtime.
